items.body:
Tom Parker Creamery is expanding its growing portfolio of added-value whole milks with the launch of Golden Milk, a new gently spiced whole milk drink made with turmeric, cinnamon, honey and black pepper.
Developed for those seeking out natural products to support holistic health and wellness, Golden Milk features turmeric, which contains curcumin, a naturally occurring plant compound known to help reduce inflammation and support healthy liver function.  Turmeric is paired with warming cinnamon, a spice associated with aiding digestion and a healthy metabolism.
Believed to be a UK category first the 500ml ready-to-drink Golden Milk will launch into Waitrose and Ocado from 21 October, joining Tom Parker Creamery’s Vitamin-Enriched Whole Milk and Bedtime Milk as the Somerset creamery continues to carve out a distinctive position in added-value and functional dairy drinks.
Made with free-range British whole milk, Golden Milk takes inspiration from the traditional turmeric-based Indian drink haldi doodh – literally “turmeric milk” – which combines warm milk with turmeric and has long been enjoyed in South Asia. Golden milk has grown in popularity driven by increasing consumer interest in natural ingredients, botanicals and food and drink associated with health and wellbeing.
The launch builds on a wider consumer shift towards whole foods, recognisable ingredients and minimally processed products – trends that Tom Parker Creamery has increasingly placed at the heart of its proposition. Its existing added-value milk portfolio includes Vitamin-Enriched Whole Milk and Bedtime Milk, with the creamery positioning added-value dairy as an opportunity to bring new usage occasions and innovation to shake up the milk fixture.
Rob Yates, CEO of Tom Parker Creamery, said: “Consumers are increasingly looking for more from everyday food and drink, but at the same time they want products made with natural ingredients they recognise. We think dairy is brilliantly placed to respond to both trends.
“Golden Milk brings together our free-range British whole milk with turmeric, cinnamon, honey and black pepper to create something that supports wellbeing as part of a healthy lifestyle. It’s a simple, delicious drink that can be enjoyed chilled straight from the fridge or gently warmed, opening up another occasion for whole milk beyond the traditional breakfast table.”
Golden Milk follows the successful development of Tom Parker Creamery’s added-value milk range, including its Vitamin-Enriched Whole Milk and Bedtime Milk, launched in 2025. The latter helped establish the brand in functional dairy, combining whole milk with botanicals and tapping into growing consumer interest in food and drink that fits into wider wellbeing routines. Tom Parker Creamery has previously identified “adding value to the milk category” and developing milks enriched with natural ingredients as an important part of its evolving brand proposition.
The new product retains the hallmarks of the wider Tom Parker Creamery range, including British whole milk and the brand’s distinctive glass bottle packaging with recyclable paper labels.

As UK shoppers hunt for Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals, retailers face growing pressure to win their Christmas spending. New PayPal research reveals that nine in ten (91%) are taking steps to manage festive costs, including 27% waiting for sales and promotions. But price isn’t the only factor influencing where they shop. More than […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
As UK shoppers hunt for Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals, retailers face growing pressure to win their Christmas spending. New PayPal research reveals that nine in ten (91%) are taking steps to manage festive costs, including 27% waiting for sales and promotions. But price isn’t the only factor influencing where they shop. More than half (55%) of Christmas shoppers using Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) would favour a retailer showing the option on product pages, highlighting the opportunity for retailers to attract customers by making payment choices clear earlier.
Savvy Brits are also comparing prices to find cheaper deals (35%), while a third (33%) have already used or plan to use BNPL for Christmas shopping this year. Consumers value spreading purchases over time (55%) and knowing in advance how payments will be divided (55%).
Technology is also changing how shoppers prepare for Christmas. More than a third (35%) have used or plan to use AI for Christmas shopping, while 52% say they would use AI to find deals or compare prices. As shoppers research and compare purchases, retailers have an opportunity to make payment options just as visible as prices and promotions.
PayPal’s research reveals retailers can influence buying decisions by sharing payment options earlier in the shopping journey. More than half of British shoppers (53%) start thinking about payment by the time they are browsing products, while more than two-thirds (69%) of Christmas BNPL shoppers want to know the option is available by the product page. In fact, two-thirds (67%) say seeing BNPL on a product page would make them more likely to add an item to their basket this Christmas.
For JTX Fitness, a UK home fitness retailer, understanding those needs is particularly relevant when customers are weighing up a considered purchase.
Jamie Forshaw, head of marketing at JTX Fitness, said: “Promoting PayPal Pay Later1 earlier in the customer journey has been a real driver of growth for our business. A treadmill or exercise bike is a considered purchase, so showing customers their payment options while they’re still browsing can help them feel more confident about how they’ll manage the cost.
“Getting our payment strategy right before checkout has made a real difference. When customers can see Pay Later from the product page onwards, more of them go from browsing to buying, and that has helped us grow.”
Sean Douglas, senior director of UK large enterprise at PayPal, said: “Peak shopping season can feel like a time when retailers just need to survive, but it can be so much more. Our data shows merchants that made Pay Later more visible saw an 11% uplift in PayPal payment volumes within three months2. That could be the difference in meeting revenue targets, which is a success in itself, or smashing them out of the park… I know which I’d choose.”
About PayPal Pay Later
PayPal Pay Later gives eligible customers flexibility in how they pay. Merchants can display Pay Later messaging across the shopping journey, including on product pages, helping customers understand the payment options available while they are still considering a purchase.
Retailers can find out how to add and optimise PayPal Pay Later messaging across the shopping journey at https://www.paypal.com/uk/campaign/pay-later.

items.body:
Asda is celebrating 10 years of stocking Arla Farmers Milk, marking a decade of giving shoppers the opportunity to provide additional support to dairy farmers through their everyday milk purchases.
Since launching in 2016, sales of Arla Farmers Milk have generated more than £7 million in additional returns for Arla farmers. For every bottle sold, an additional 25p is returned to Arla Foods’ farmer-owned cooperative, providing extra support for farmers.
The milestone reflects not only the success of Arla Farmers Milk, but also the strength of the long-standing partnership between Asda and Arla. Over more than a decade, the retailer has worked with Arla to support farmers, while giving shoppers a clear and transparent way to contribute additional support through their purchase of Farmers Milk.
Rebecca Stanton, business unit director – Chilled said: “We’re incredibly proud to celebrate 10 years of Arla Farmers Milk at Asda. Thanks to the support of our customers, the partnership has returned more than £7 million to Arla farmers, demonstrating the positive impact long-term partnerships can have on British dairy farming. It’s a fantastic milestone for Asda, Arla and the farmers who supply our milk.”
Jonathan Dixon, SVP of sales for Arla Foods UK, comments: “As a farmer-owned cooperative, creating value for our farmer owners is at the heart of everything we do. For 10 years, Arla Farmers Milk has given Asda shoppers a clear and simple way to provide additional support to farmers through their purchase. The fact that this has generated more than £7 million in additional returns over the past decade is something we are incredibly proud of, and demonstrates the value of long-term partnerships between farmers, retailers and shoppers.”
The milestone comes as Asda continues the rollout of Daisy the Cow across its estate, after the iconic 90s in-store character recently returned to stores as part of the retailer’s programme to enhance the in-store experience and drive engagement within key categories.
Arla Farmers Milk is sold in both Whole and Semi-Skimmed 4-pint formats.

items.body:
Asda is expanding its no and low alcohol offering with the launch of Balancing Act, a new
own-brand, exclusive wine range designed for customers seeking greater balance in their lifestyles without compromising on taste or quality.
With party season fast approaching, the range offers more choice when it comes to celebrating and entertaining, perfect for those looking to moderate alcohol or try something new.
The new collection launches with three wines across two price tiers, offering shoppers a choice of budget-friendly (£6.00) and more premium (£10.00) options.
Developed in partnership with one of Asda’s premium French wine suppliers in the renowned Loire Valley, the wines have been carefully crafted to retain the authentic flavour profile and character of the grapes, while significantly reducing alcohol content.
The range includes the Balancing Act Sauvignon Blanc 0.0% ABV (£6.00) – a more budget-friendly option for modern drinkers, with notes of aromatic white fruits, citrus, white flowers and a vibrant acidity that makes it a perfectly balanced wine.
The more premium version, the Balancing Act Sauvignon Blanc 0.5% ABV (£10.00) is an elevated, elegant and fresh white wine, with white fruit, pear, and cherry blossom notes on the palate, and subtle vanilla notes on the finish from oak aging.
The red star of the show in the range, then Balancing Act Pinot Noir 0.5% ABV (£10.00), has aromas of red cherries and strawberries, elevated by hints of spice and subtle oak, bringing structure and complexity to a low alcohol red wine.
The name Balancing Act, exclusively at Asda, reflects both the winemaking expertise required to preserve a wine’s character without alcohol, and the modern lifestyles of consumers who are increasingly looking to balance social occasions with mindful drinking choices, especially in the run up to the festive period.
Tom Bourne, wine sourcing manager at Asda, said: “The no and low category continues to evolve rapidly, but finding wines that truly deliver on quality and varietal character remains a challenge. With Balancing Act, we’ve worked closely with our winemaking partner in the Loire Valley to create wines that offer a genuine step up in quality.”
“The range is all about balance. It’s about balancing the craft of winemaking with alcohol reduction, while also recognising that many customers want to enjoy great wine as part of a more balanced lifestyle. Whether they’re cutting back completely or simply moderating during many social events in the run up to the festive period, we wanted to offer wines that don’t feel like a compromise.”
Asda’s Balancing Act range is available in Asda stores and online at Asda.com now.

Christmas lunch is back on the menu as Co-op’s much-loved festive sandwiches return to stores nationwide from October 21st.
The Christmas sandwich is the ultimate lunchtime treat, and this year, Co-op is introducing two exciting newcomers to the range as well as bringing back some of its fan favourites, all made with quality ingredients.
Returning to shelves this year are four highly anticipated lines: Turkey Feast, Boxing Day Feast, Pigs Under Blankets and Brie & Cranberry, all packed with the classic festive flavours shoppers know and love.
As part of the retailer’s long-standing commitment to backing British farming, all its own brand meat is 100% British, including fresh turkey in its core sandwich range.
Shoppers looking to try something new will find two premium additions landing from December 2nd – a Christmas Club Sandwich bringing together some of the season’s most-loved festive flavours, and a Posh Prawn Cocktail Sandwich with succulent king prawns and a zesty Marie Rose sauce, reminiscent of the nation’s much loved seasonal starter.
The range is also available as part of Co-op’s lunchtime meal deals, priced at £3.85 for members (£4.25 for non-members), while premium options are included in the Premium Meal Deal priced at £5.50 for members (£6 for non-members).
Helen Jagger, product development manager for Food to Go, said: “For many shoppers, the arrival of Christmas sandwiches is the moment the festive season really begins. We know our customers look forward to picking up their favourites every year, which is why we’re bringing back our most-loved classics. And for those keen to try something new, we’ll also introduce two exciting premium additions we’re sure will be a hit when they land in December.”
Proceeds from Co-op’s core Christmas sandwiches will be donated to Barnardo’s* as part of its national partnership which has already raised more than £7 million and supported positive futures for one million young people across the UK. Over the past decade, this range alone has raised more than £500,000 for Co-op’s national charity partners.

Creamy Brie cheese, sweet cranberry chutney, seasoned mayonnaise, and spinach on malted bread. An un-brie-lievable combo!

items.body:
As consumers increasingly seek out convenient, protein-rich foods that fit around busy lifestyles, the happy egg co. is expanding its offer with four new chilled products launching in Tesco stores nationwide.
Available from 12th October, the new range includes: Mozzarella & Tomato Egg Bites (RRP £3); Ham Hock with Sweet Potato Frittata Slices (RRP £3); Boiled Eggs (6 pack) (RRP £3.50) and Poached Eggs (4 pack) (RRP £3.50).
The launch sees the happy egg co. bring its trusted egg brand into new chilled formats, helping consumers enjoy eggs wherever and whenever they choose.
Long loved by families for their taste, versatility and value, eggs are increasingly being enjoyed beyond traditional breakfast occasions. Developed in partnership with Tesco, the new range has been designed to help consumers enjoy eggs throughout the day, whether that’s a grab-and-go breakfast, a satisfying afternoon snack, a quick lunch or an easy meal solution.
The launch supports Noble Foods’ wider ambition to help more people enjoy eggs on more occasions by bringing the quality, taste and versatility consumers already know from the happy egg co. into convenient chilled formats developed to suit modern lifestyles.
James Howes, brand marketing manager at Noble Foods, said: “People already love eggs because they’re tasty, versatile and easy to enjoy in so many different ways. As lifestyles become busier, we’re seeing growing demand for products that make those benefits even more accessible, while also delivering the nutritional qualities consumers increasingly value.”
“Working closely with Tesco, we’ve developed a range that gives shoppers even more opportunities to choose eggs throughout the day. Whether it’s breakfast, lunch, snacking or an easier evening meal, these products bring the trusted quality of the happy egg co. into formats that fit naturally into people’s lives.”
The launch comes during a period of continued growth for Noble Foods’ added-value portfolio. Alongside the continued expansion of the happy egg co. beyond shell eggs, including last year’s frozen omelette launch, the business has also recently introduced Kudos, a brand focused on rewarding nutrition and protein-rich eating occasions. Together, the two brands are helping Noble Foods serve a broader range of consumer needs, from trusted family favourites through to nutrition-led choices.
Behind the launch is significant investment in Noble Foods’ growing added-value business. Since opening in 2024, the company’s Leicester facility has doubled in capacity, reflecting increasing demand for convenient egg products and providing a platform for future innovation.

items.title: Cost crisis looms for independent retailers unless chancellor acts in Budget, says Bira
items.summary: Independent retailers face a looming cost crisis unless the chancellor announces action on business rates, employment costs and energy bills in the upcoming Budget, the British Independent Retailers Association (Bira) has warned. Bira, which works with over 6,000 independent retailers across the UK, says shop… This story continues at Cost crisis looms for independent retailers unless chancellor acts in Budget, says Bira Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Bira, which works with over 6,000 independent retailers across the UK, says shop owners are increasingly nervous as the Budget on 28 October approaches, with tight margins set to be squeezed further.
Bira said it has welcomed reports that the chancellor plans to fund business rates cuts by making online marketplaces collect VAT, and is urging him to confirm that the money raised goes directly to rates relief for high street shops.
Andrew Goodacre, CEO of Bira, said: “We appreciate that the economy is challenging and the chancellor has limited room to manoeuvre, but independent retailers will have even less headroom if support is not forthcoming in the Budget.
“Rates, employment and energy costs are all heading in the wrong direction, and independent retailers need to see action on all three.”
Bira warns that, without action in the Budget, the average independent retailer faces a business rates bill next year that is 25% higher than this year, before inflation is added.
Goodacre said: “Such an increase is simply not sustainable in the current climate. Many independent retailers are already operating on the finest of margins, and a rise on this scale could be the difference between keeping the doors open and closing for good.”
The association is also calling for action on employment costs. Bira says the cost of employment has risen significantly over the past two years, a period in which the retail sector has lost around 100,000 jobs, and the increases in employer National Insurance contributions continue to weigh heavily on smaller businesses.
Goodacre added: “The NIC increases are still damaging. If we want to create opportunities for younger people in independent retail, the government needs to increase the Employment Allowance to reduce the cost of employment.
“Independent shops are often where young people get their first job, learn customer service and build the confidence to develop a career. We cannot afford to lose those opportunities.”
On energy, Bira is warning of a tough winter ahead, with prices set to rise. The association wants smaller businesses to have access to more flexible energy contracts, allowing them to switch suppliers and shop around for a better deal in the same way as domestic customers.
Goodacre said: “Too many small businesses are locked into rigid energy contracts with little room to move when prices change.”
“They should have the same freedom as domestic users to shop around. Giving independent retailers that flexibility would make a real difference to their ability to manage costs this winter.”
“This Budget is an opportunity to show independent retailers that the government is on their side. Action on business rates, employment costs and energy would give them the headroom they need to invest, employ and keep our high streets thriving.”

items.title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
items.summary: Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demand Business live – latest updates Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending. China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%. Continue reading...
items.body:
Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.
China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.
China’s economy has now grown by 4.6% in the first nine months of the year, putting it on track to hit the government’s 2026 target of 4.5%-5% growth without extra stimulus measures.
Industrial production rose 5.5% in September, up from 5.2% in August, while retail sales only increased 1.1%, up from 0.4%.
Duncan Wrigley, the chief China economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, said Beijing’s policymakers were likely to conclude that their efforts to stabilise headline growth in the third quarter were successful.
“Headline industrial production rose in September partly as coalmines resumed operations after safety inspections prompted by a major accident. Manufacturing output growth remained robust at 6.0% year on year in September, buoyed up by stronger export demand for electronics, AI-related equipment and autos,” Wrigley said.
“Hi-tech manufacturing output continues to outperform traditional sectors, as China climbs the value-added ladder,” Wrigley added.
However, fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% over the first nine months, property investment tumbled by 20.6%, and infrastructure spending remained weak.
Data last week showed that China’s exports surged by more than a third in September, lifted by a rise in shipments of electronics related to AI.
“This pickup in GDP growth mainly reflects ongoing export strength on the global AI/tech boom, more than offsetting drags from the Iran conflict and ongoing weakness in domestic demand,” said analysts at ABN Amro.

items.body:
Former Amazon and M&S executive Murray Beckett bags Director of Omnichannel & Retail Media role at Boots
Murray Beckett has started a new role as Director of Omnichannel & Retail Media at Boots. He was previously at Amazon where he served as GM, Marketing/Digital - EMEA & APAC. His CV also includes stints at Boohoo Group, Nike, and Marks and Spencer.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “Just a few days in, I'm grateful for the warm welcome I've received and looking forward to learning, meeting more of the team, and playing a small part in our mission to help people live healthier, longer, happier lives.”
He added: “One thing that has been reinforced since the interview process is how much pride there is in the business: its heritage, success, and the role it plays in customers' lives. There's also a noticeable sense of anticipation right now. With new leadership and ownership, it feels like people are energised by the opportunities ahead. Care x Commerce. I reckon that's a Bootiful thing.”
TikTok Shop
Boots UK has kicked off a TikTok Shop pilot, in partnership with THG Commerce, involving a curated selection of No7 skincare and beauty products. Further brands and products are set to launch over the coming months.
Paula Bobbett, Chief Digital and Data Officer at Boots, says: “Millions of people are already discovering beauty and skincare products through TikTok and the creators and communities that they trust. This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.”
Daniel Callaghan, Business Development Manager at THG Ingenuity, says: “Boots' debut on TikTok Shop is a testament to the growth and development that the platform has seen over the last few years. This forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bring beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, it aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop. Huge move, and well done to everyone involved.”

Earlier this year, Pop Mart opened its largest London store to date, unveiling a new retail destination in the heart of the West End. Located at 69–71 Charing Cross Road (WC2H 0NE), this spans 5,090 square feet and introduces a mezzanine level, a first for a Pop Mart store in the UK.
Situated in the former home of House of Spells and close to the brand’s first London store in Soho, the Charing Cross Road addition marked Pop Mart's 16th store in the UK. It boosted ts London presence with seven standalone stores and nine London locations overall, including dedicated spaces within Harrods and Hamleys. It has since shuttered its Soho location.
Ian Ashton, Head of UK Retail at Pop Mart, said: "The growth of our London community has been incredible, and this store is a reflection of that momentum. Charing Cross Road is more than a retail space - it’s where the Pop Mart universe comes to life, bringing together collectors, creativity and culture in one destination. This opening is about giving our community a home, while inviting new fans to discover what makes Pop Mart so unique."
Opening under the theme Step Into the Magic, the location introduced the Twinkle Twinkle Fairground, an immersive experience designed to spark curiosity and bring Pop Mart’s characters to life.

items.body:
PMC and Deliverect among 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Tech Implementation of the Year (UK) finalists
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Technology Implementation of the Year (UK) category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Technology Implementation of the Year (UK) finalists as follows:
Ann Summers and PMC
Ann Summers partnered with PMC to modernise its core IT infrastructure after years of legacy development had left its tech stack complicated, expensive to maintain and difficult to manage, slowing innovation and creating operational friction.
Asda and Deliverect
Deliverect has partnered with Asda Express to simplify on-demand retail operations across its estate, consolidating separate Uber Eats, Deliveroo and Just Eat picking workflows into one unified application.
Rolled out across the Asda Express estate, the technology gives store teams a single process for managing and picking marketplace orders, reducing operational complexity while significantly improving product availability and picking accuracy. The simpler experience has also driven improved staff NPS. Beyond operational efficiency, the initiative provides the technology infrastructure underpinning Asda Express's q-commerce success, creating a scalable ecosystem where additional digital channels and capabilities can be introduced easily as and when required.
cardfactory and Retail Response
In autumn 2025 and spring 2026, cardfactory entrusted Retail Response with two ambitious, estate wide technology roll-outs. The first upgraded legacy PoS software across the estate, creating the foundation for a complete payment’s technology refresh delivered the following spring.
Across both programmes, Retail Response completed two store visits per location over 16 weeks, with roll-out activity peaking at approximately 40 stores per day. Delivered at exceptional pace and scale, the programmes modernised cardfactory’s retail technology infrastructure while minimising disruption to trading. Together, they demonstrate how careful planning, technical expertise and outstanding execution can deliver complex transformation.
Castore and Patchworks
Castore, the multi-brand fashion and apparel retailer, runs 35 Shopify stores across multiple regions. At peak, its pricing process was manual and fragile: two people spent 6–7 hours a night importing CSVs into NetSuite, success rates were only 60–70%, and the ERP was pushed past safe concurrency limits.
Castore redesigned the flow so approved pricing moves from SharePoint into Snowflake, is validated and signed off, then delivered straight to Shopify by Patchworks. Pricing updates fell from around five hours to 2–3 minutes, error rates dropped from 30–35% to 1–2%, and peak ran with zero error days.
East of England Co-op and Transaction Network Services (TNS)
Transaction Network Services (TNS) delivered a fully managed TNS Secure SD-WAN implementation across East of England Co-op's estate of more than 200 grocery, travel and funeral sites in Norfolk, Suffolk and Essex.
The project consolidated fragmented, multi-vendor connectivity into a single, resilient network with built-in redundancy, reducing failover from up to 90 seconds to instantaneous. Centralised dashboards now provide real-time, estate wide visibility, strengthening compliance and security oversight. Delivered by a dedicated TNS account team with clear project leadership and ownership, the implementation has produced estimated operational savings of 10-15% and zero visible downtime during failover events.
Great Northern Market, Manchester Airport T2
Vita Mojo powers every order at Airport Retail Enterprises' Great Northern Market, the first street food market of its kind in a UK airport, at Manchester Airport Terminal 2.
The three-floor market brings together six kitchens, a bakery, two bars and four kiosks as one unified operation. An Order & Pay at Table model lets passengers browse multiple vendors and pay in a single transaction, with orders routed dynamically across 13 operational flows and six menus. Vita Mojo worked consultatively with Airport Retail Enterprises from concept through launch, delivering a go-live with zero operational issues.
Iceland and SAI
Facing approximately £20 million in annual retail losses from theft and shoplifting, Iceland sought a scalable way to reduce shrink without increasing labour costs or introducing additional hardware to its estate, as well as ensuring it didn’t add friction for honest customers.
Working with SAI, Iceland deployed an AI powered loss prevention platform across its existing store cameras, providing real-time detection of theft events across checkouts, store aisles and exits. The solution enabled colleagues to intervene quickly and safely through highly accurate alerts, delivered directly to handheld devices.
John Lewis and FoundIt!
FoundIt! is an AI driven, intent led commerce platform helping major retailers transform how customers discover, navigate and buy products. Its technology turns millions of behavioural, search and product signals into scalable customer journeys, visual navigation, richer product data and SEO structures aligned to genuine shopper intent.
Working with retailers including John Lewis, B&Q and M&S, FoundIt! has moved AI beyond experimentation and into live enterprise commerce environments. The platform delivers measurable customer and commercial outcomes, including eight-figure benefits, while helping retailers prepare for search and shopping increasingly shaped by AI agents.
LeMieux
LeMieux Insiders was launched in November 2025 to transform a high growth equestrian brand into a community led, loyalty powered ecosystem that builds meaningful, long-term customer relationships beyond transactional commerce.
WHSmith and SOLUM
Waitrose and SOLUM are delivering a nationwide digital shelf transformation using Newton Pro electronic shelf labels. Following pilots, the programme has expanded to more than 200 stores and over three million labels.
Centrally managed digital displays enable faster, more consistent updates across fresh, ambient and specialist categories. By reducing repetitive ticket changes, the programme helps Partners focus more on products and customers while maintaining the premium store experience expected from the Home of Food Lovers.

items.body:
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Technology Implementation of the Year (Rest of World) finalists announced
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Technology Implementation of the Year (Rest of World) category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Technology Implementation of the Year (Rest of World) finalists as follows:
Davines and Attensi
Davines and Attensi transformed launch readiness from locally delivered, inconsistently measured training into a scalable global sales-enablement capability.
For the Beautiful Things launch, game-based simulations gave Davines’ international sales community repeated, practical product practice, while a jointly developed evaluation framework connected engagement with sales performance.
Despite being voluntary and spanning employees and independent distributors, the programme achieved 74% participation and 56% completion; four of six direct sales countries reached 100% for both. Learners training for more than 30 minutes recorded higher median sales, with analysis identifying a potential €320,000 uplift. The programme has since expanded into additional launches and capability building initiatives.
EDEKA and GEBOS
EDEKA, Germany's largest food retailer, is a cooperative of around 3,200 independent retailers and seven regional companies, with a highly diverse store estate.
Driven by moving over half of its checkouts from Windows to Linux, GEBOS, GEBIT's InStore Operating System, has been in production in every regional company since September 2026, in company owned and independent stores alike. More than 900 PoS and back-end devices are managed from one central platform, in a single tenant, across all regions.
Results: PoS and server hardware from nine manufacturers, new devices checkout ready in under 30 minutes, 99% on the current release.
Fynd
A leading quick service restaurant operator set out to run its entire business across web, app and kiosk on one engine that keeps meal deals, pricing, localisation and loyalty consistent everywhere.
Partnering with Fynd, it rebuilt the experience on a single platform covering bundling, localisation, a central catalogue, loyalty, promotions, new ordering formats and multilingual AI support. Since going fully live on Fynd Commerce, daily orders have grown a sustained 7.0% over the pre-Fynd baseline, holding up across the period rather than for a single week.
GEN-Y Hitch and Patchworks
GEN-Y Hitch makes premium towing and mobility accessories and sells to both retail customers and wholesale dealers. Its heavily customised WooCommerce site carried high technical debt, and script-based links to NetSuite caused data gaps, inventory variances and delayed fulfilment updates.
With implementation partner Shero Commerce, GEN-Y moved to Shopify for D2C and B2B (via SparkLayer), with Patchworks as the integration layer to NetSuite. Patchworks automates SKU and variant alignment, real-time stock sync and order routing. The results: 75% year-on-year revenue growth, 36% lower total cost of ownership, a 100% Core Web Vitals pass rate and fully automated ERP sync.
Noken and nsign
FLO·W Experience is an immersive technology implementation delivered by nsign Managed Solutions for Noken, the bathroom brand of Porcelanosa Grupo.
Installed at Noken’s showroom in Vila-real, Spain, it transforms the future bathroom from a concept into a live, personalised journey for professional visitors. nsign served as AV integrator, hardware supplier and installer, deploying its CMS and media players as the content orchestration layer connecting NFC identification, sensors and Loxone automation.
Pharma&Go and Sensei
Pharma&GO is a 100% autonomous health and wellbeing store in Lisbon, open 24/7 with no staff on site. Opened in November 2025 opposite Hospital CUF Descobertas, it was delivered by Pharma&GO with Glintt Life and technology partner Sensei.
Customers check in with a bank card, pick up products and walk out; payment is automatic. Computer vision and in-shelf scales track every item in real time, with anonymous processing and no facial recognition. In its first three months the 70 m² store recorded more than 7,200 visits, averaging three minutes each, and proved a model for hybrid pharmacies.
Quorso
Quorso is an AI powered intelligent management platform for large-format grocery, convenience, apparel, and specialty retailers. It turns fragmented store data into a daily set of actions store teams can actually take.
Rather than another dashboard, Quorso identifies the highest impact opportunity in every store, every day, and delivers it as a specific mission with a clear reason and a measurable outcome. In the last three months alone, store teams completed more than 800,000 missions across sales, inventory and shrink, people and operations.
TCS
A leading European grocery retailer faced growing business constraints from a legacy integration landscape that was expensive to maintain, difficult to scale, and slowing digital transformation efforts. TCS EventForge introduced an AI powered modernisation approach that rapidly converts legacy integrations into a modern, real-time operating model. The initiative reduced dependency on specialist resources, accelerated transformation timelines, and enabled a phased, low risk migration strategy.
With live deployments in production, EventForge is helping the retailer modernise faster, improve operational agility, and unlock significant cost savings while building a future ready foundation for innovation and growth.

items.body:
Miniso set to replace HMV on London’s Oxford Street with opening of 19,000 sq ft flagship store
Miniso is gearing up to open its first Miniso Land store in the UK. The 19,000 sq ft flagship will be located at 363 Oxford Street, London, currently occupied by HMV, and will line up alongside the retailer’s other flagship stores, which includes New York’s Times Square and Paris’s Champs-Élysées, alongside over 8,300 stores globally.
Sam Foyle, Co-head of Global Retail at Savills, which acted for the landlord, says: “We’re seeing continued interest from brands for space on Oxford Street. Pedestrianisation plans have really fuelled momentum over the past year and, as the street enters a more mature stage of recovery, we expect this appetite to continue.”
“Oxford Street is a microcosm of the UK high street, where brands are increasingly focused on creating memorable, experience led destinations. Miniso Land is a great example of that trend, bringing an innovative flagship concept to one of the world’s most recognisable retail locations. Its decision to open at 363 Oxford Street is a strong vote of confidence in London and reinforces Oxford Street’s appeal as a destination for ambitious global brands.”
A Miniso spokesperson says: “London is an important part of our international growth, and bringing Miniso Land to Oxford Street marks an exciting next step. The flagship reflects our long-term commitment to the UK and our ambition to connect people with the characters and stories they love and bring joy to everyday life.”
Earlier this month, HMV announced it intended to vacate the site in March 2027 after three years. It first launched the Oxford Street site in 1921 and reopened it in late 2023 following a four-year absence.

items.body:
Jysk brings unified commerce to UK&I and Ikea gets digital in China: last week’s biggest retail technology plays
RTIH rounds up the stand out retail technology deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including Foot Locker, Morrisons, B&Q, Bluffworks, Frasers Group, Tesco Media, JULES, Footasylum, Fortenova Group, M&S, e.l.f. Cosmetics, and Ann Summers.
Foot Locker
Foot Locker has developed, in partnership with Stylitics, a new AI powered closet builder, Fits, within its mobile app. In a LinkedIn post, Michael Cera, Interim Head of Product Management and Design at Foot Locker, said: “AI is everywhere. But, at Foot Locker, we challenged ourselves to think about how to improve and make positive change to our customers shopping experience through the use of AI.”
He added: “We engaged with customers, really listened, and in partnership with Stylitics, developed a key new closet builder within the Foot Locker app - let me introduce you to Fits! Start with something you own. Discover personalised outfits built around it. See those looks come to life on a virtual model.”
Customers can upload or take a photo of something they own, discover complete outfits built around it, and visualise those looks on a virtual model. Paired with a cart addition from the model view, the aim is to make purchasing a whole outfit styled around your own products that much easier.
Cera concluded: “This was a collaborative effort across Experience Design, Product Management, E-comm, Brand, and Stylitics, and came to life exactly as we all set out to do. Download or open your Foot Locker app today and give it a try!”
B&Q
B&Q is ramping up its fast delivery push with the launch of TradePoint Express, a same-day delivery service exclusively for trade customers, in partnership with Gophr. The retailer has also expanded its Deliveroo partnership to more than 100 stores nationwide following a trial. Customers can now access up to more than 9,000 home improvement products through Deliveroo, with orders delivered in as little as 35 minutes.
The partnership with Gophr will allow Business Development Managers to arrange deliveries, either within two hours or for a pre-booked two-hour slot same-day, for TradePoint members from B&Q's standalone TradePoint store in Barking and 123 participating B&Q stores across the UK. The service is set to expand to all TradePoint stores later this year.
The launch builds on the introduction of Marketplace Click & Collect. Customers can now choose from an expanding range of collection and delivery options designed to suit planned projects, urgent repairs and last minute requirements.
Footasylum
THG Fulfil recently completed its first AutoStore implementation for an external retailer. Footasylum’s automated fulfilment operation is now live and delivering 212% of the output of the retailer’s previous operation, from fewer than half the picking stations.
Announced in June, the system processed its first customer order on 28th August and went fully live on 14th September. According to those involved, the build was delivered two months faster than the original project plan, with less than six months between contract signature and first order. A fleet of 85 AutoStore R5 robots operates across 96,000 bin locations, with 100% of Footasylum’s live SKU range stored in the grid and system uptime holding at 99.8%.
Before construction began, the two teams ran 80,000 simulations using Footasylum’s order history, seasonal demand curves and product data to determine the optimum number of robots and ports. At the heart of the live operation is THG Fulfil’s proprietary Warehouse Control System (WCS), developed over five years inside its own AutoStore network. Its in-house development team is refining the WCS after go-live, using live order data to improve bin sequencing, batching and stock positioning.
The project was delivered under a hybrid commercial model combining elements of capital investment and THG Fulfil’s robotics-as-a-service (RaaS) offering, structured specifically around Footasylum’s requirements.
Primepick
Primepick, a New York-based company that designs and manufactures robotic food kiosks, reports that it is expanding to new locations. The startup is bringing MealMate, an unattended kiosk that serves hot dishes in five to seven minutes, to a hospital and a nursing home in the Tri-State area, its fourth and fifth sites. Primepick is also preparing three new deployments in Huntsville, Chicago and Dallas.
These installations follow earlier ones at manufacturing sites in New Jersey and Connecticut and at Molloy University. For hospitals, manufacturing facilities and other round-the-clock environments, MealMate provides access to complete hot meals beyond traditional foodservice hours, without requiring an on-site kitchen or additional foodservice staff. At the aforementioned university, students order hot meals between classes and late into the evening, including dishes from local BBQ and Asian restaurants.
M&S
Klarna reports that it is now available as a payment option at Marks & Spencer for fashion, home and beauty purchases online. Shoppers on M&S.com and the UK retailer’s app can now tap Klarna and split the cost into three equal, interest free payments with, according to a press release, transparent terms and no revolving balance.
"People deserve flexibility without paying interest for it, so our goal is simple: meet them wherever they shop," says Klarna Head of UK, Ireland & Western & Southern Europe, Raji Behal. "M&S is a beloved British icon that brings second to none quality and value to millions of shoppers every day. We’re proud to now offer them a transparent way to spread the cost with no interest and a clear end date."
Katherine Carlson, Director of Financial Services at M&S, says: “We are always looking for ways to make it easier for our customers to shop with us. Customers shopping on M&S.com and through our app can now spread the cost in three interest free payments with Klarna, offering more flexibility in how they pay for the things they love.”
Orange
Pricer has been selected by Orange, a telecommunications operator in France, to digitalise its retail store network. The project encompasses 561 stores with an average size of 120 m² over the next two years.
The agreement covers the complete deployment of Pricer’s electronic shelf label (ESL) solution, including hardware, infrastructure, attachment solutions, installation, and cloud management via the Plaza platform under a long-term maintenance contract. It includes annual recurring SaaS and maintenance revenue. Orange chose Pricer following pilot programmes across multiple store locations.
Morrisons
Morrisons has selected Logile as it looks to enhance store workload planning across the UK grocery retailer’s business. The agreement covers its supermarket and convenience store estate alongside its logistics network.
Morrisons is implementing Logile software in a bid to simplify central planning, replacing time-consuming manual spreadsheets with optimised operational data and intelligence. By delivering clearer visibility into store workload requirements, it says that central operations can provide accurate, reliable insight across the estate, allowing teams to focus on better supporting store operations.
“Getting colleagues where customers need them most is the heart of what we do, and at our scale you need a reliable, shared foundation to get that right,” says Alex Rose, Head of Productivity at Morrisons. “A large supermarket and a local convenience store operate differently so our planning has to flex to those local needs while keeping central support consistent. When our store managers have plans they can depend on, they spend less time managing admin and more time supporting their colleagues and serving customers.”
Bluffworks
Travel apparel brand, Bluffworks, has selected Cart.com as its exclusive US fulfilment partner. Its inventory and fulfillment operations are now centralised at Cart.com’s Terrell, Texas facility. Bluffworks expects the new operation to lower its fulfilment costs by at least 20%.
"I've spent my career on both sides of logistics, first building supply chain systems as a software developer and then relying on them to run a brand," says Stefan Loble, Founder and CEO at Bluffworks. "I am still stunned at how different the accuracy, cost and level of service can be between two large, similar looking fulfilment providers.”
“Cart.com has their operation buttoned up, especially their technology. I can open their software and see the status of the whole operation without emailing anyone to ask. When something goes wrong, like a shipment turning up damaged, which happens in this business, you find out fast whether you’re in good hands on the other end. With Cart.com we are."
Ann Summers
InPost has partnered with Ann Summers with the retailer’s customers now able to choose 48-hour delivery to an InPost parcel locker at checkout, select a location and collect at a time that suits them. They will also be able to make returns through InPost’s network of over 16,000 lockers.
Jon Nicholson, Chief Commercial Officer, InPost UK, comments: “Ann Summers has spent decades disrupting the high street and empowering its customers, while InPost is challenging the way delivery has traditionally worked. Bringing those two mindsets together makes this a really exciting partnership. Customers expect choice throughout the shopping journey, and delivery should be no different.”
“By adding InPost locker delivery, Ann Summers is giving its customers greater freedom to choose the location and collection time that works best for them. For retailers, delivery is an increasingly important part of the overall customer experience. Giving people more options at checkout creates a more flexible, modern shopping journey, and that is exactly where InPost continues to push the category forward.”
Maria Hollins, CEO, Ann Summers, says: “For more than 50 years, we have pushed boundaries and championed empowerment, confidence and choice for our customers. Our partnership with InPost brings that same approach into another part of the shopping journey, giving our customers even greater freedom over how and where they receive their orders. We want every interaction with us to feel empowering and on our customers’ terms. InPost locker delivery gives them another simple and flexible option, putting even more choice into their hands.”
Fortenova Group
Hanshow, a Chinese specialist in digital store solutions, has partnered with Kenty Adria, a member of Fortenova Group, to support the large scale roll-out of electronic shelf labels (ESL) across Konzum and Mercator stores in Croatia and Slovenia. Building on pilot projects, the deployment forms part of the broader digital transformation of Fortenova Group's retail network.
At Konzum, electronic pricing has been introduced in more than 200 stores, with a further 260 stores planned for deployment. The largest implementation to date includes 44,000 electronic shelf labels installed at Konzum’s store on Radnička Street in Zagreb. The majority of its retail network, comprising more than 600 stores across Croatia, is expected to be equipped by the end of the 2027 summer season.
At Mercator, electronic shelf labels have so far been installed in 50 stores across Slovenia, with the goal of deploying ESL solutions throughout the entire Mercator retail network by the end of 2027. Across the network, the full roll-out is estimated to require approximately 3.1 million ESLs.
e.l.f. Cosmetics
e.l.f. Cosmetics, which is part of e.l.f. Beauty, has landed on ZEPETO, an avatar-based social metaverse platform. It has launched Express your e.l.f. where players can discover the beauty trends shaping culture and turn them into complete virtual looks from head to toe.
“As a different kind of company, e.l.f. does not see boundaries between where beauty lives and where culture happens. From Twitch to Roblox and now ZEPETO, we meet our community where they like to play and give them a platform to fuel discovery, empowerment and self-expression. Every immersive experience we build is an extension of the same vision that drives everything we do: disrupt norms, shape culture and connect communities through positivity, inclusivity and accessibility,” says Patrick O’Keefe, Chief Integrated Marketing Officer, e.l.f. Brands.
ZEPETO players can now dress their avatars in e.l.f. designed digital looks with makeup from the brand’s Power Grip family and hairstyles, bags, jewellery and special effects items inspired by Power Grip’s colours and textures. Players can also show off their e.l.f. looks by snapping photos and videos against custom backgrounds and sharing them to the ZEPETO feed.
“By seamlessly blending e.l.f. Cosmetics’ iconic products with the year’s most defining trends, ZEPETO is making it possible to reimagine makeup as a comprehensive head to toe virtual styling. We are thrilled to pioneer these full looks designed by e.l.f., delivering a revolutionary brand experience that pushes the boundaries of virtual self-expression,” says Annette Lee, Head of Business Development, ZEPETO.
Ikea
Ingka Group has launched an Ikea Douyin official flagship store in China. The new digital touchpoint will offer more than 6,500 Ikea products across 179 categories, with delivery available in 301 cities across China.
The move brings the retailer in to the short-form video and content commerce platform (a sister platform to TikTok under ByteDance). The store will complement its existing stores, website, app, WeChat and other e-commerce channels in China.
Lydia Song, Ikea China Acting CEO and President and CSO, says: “People in China are increasingly moving between inspiration, discovery and shopping in ways that are highly connected and increasingly digital. Douyin E-commerce gives us an opportunity to meet people in a new context, learn what resonates with them and make Ikea more accessible to more people. This is not simply about adding another sales channel. It is about understanding how we can become part of people’s everyday lives in new and relevant ways.”
Parag Parekh, Chief Digital Officer at Ikea Retail, comments: “Retail is increasingly about being present wherever and whenever people want to meet us, while making those experiences feel like one connected Ikea. What is particularly interesting about new platforms like Douyin E-commerce is the opportunity to learn. They help us understand how inspiration, interaction and commerce are coming closer together, and what that could mean for how we continue to develop the Ikea omnichannel experience.”
Jysk
Danish home furnishing retailer Jysk reports that the first of its UK and Ireland stores are now live with its Enactor powered unified commerce platform. In a LinkedIn post, Patrick Gretsch, Retail Operations Expert at Jysk, said: "Two more countries have taken their first steps towards a new way of working, with the first stores in the UK and Ireland now successfully running on our unified commerce platform."
"I had the pleasure of joining the team at our Sallynoggin store in Ireland to experience one of these first transitions firsthand. What stood out was the excellent preparation and collaboration across all departments involved. The result? A smooth and efficient changeover, completed while the store remained open and continued serving customers."
He added: "And this is just the beginning. The roll-out is progressing at pace, with all Jysk stores in both countries expected to be running on the new platform by mid-November. So, what does this mean for our colleagues and customers? For our store teams, unified commerce means simpler processes and new opportunities to serve customers directly on the shop floor. With mobile PoS, colleagues can process payments right where the customer interaction takes place, making the shopping experience more convenient and personal."
"For our customers, it opens the door to additional services. They can, for example, order products in a store and have them delivered directly coming from our warehouse straight to their doorstep. This is what makes unified commerce so exciting: it’s not just about introducing a new platform. It’s about improving the way we work and creating new opportunities to serve our customers."
Frasers Group
Frasers Group, whose brands include Sports Direct, House of Fraser, and Flannels, reports that Antrim in Northern Ireland has become the first of its warehouses to go live with a Microsoft Dynamics 365 warehouse management system (WMS).
In a LinkedIn post, Jakob Vestergaard, Product Manager - Warehouse at Frasers Group, said: "Two years of work. One major milestone. We're live. As the first warehouse in the group to adopt D365 WMS, Antrim marks an important milestone in our wider warehouse transformation journey."
"Over the last few years, Frasers Group has invested heavily in elevating our stores. This programme is about taking the next step by elevating the warehouse operations that power them, creating a more scalable, visible and consistent platform to support our stores, brands and customers. This achievement would not have been possible without the dedication of teams across the business and our partners."
He concluded: "Go live is a major achievement, but it isn't the end of the story. Over the coming months we'll continue working with our warehouse teams, Microsoft, Binary and InterRadish to refine the solution, introduce additional capabilities and build out the global warehouse template that will support future warehouse deployments across Frasers Group. This is the first step in a much bigger journey. Looking forward to what comes next."
Tesco Media
Tesco Media has unveiled a series of new capabilities designed to help brands turn deeper customer understanding into more helpful media experiences, more connected shopping journeys and clearer proof of growth. These were announced at its 2026 Upfront event.
Key here is Ad Manager, a new client facing platform designed to make planning, booking, measuring and optimising media simpler, more connected and more useful for brands. The self-service platform gives advertisers greater control and transparency over how they work with Tesco Media, while helping them turn customer insight into action with less complexity.
Tesco Media Ad Manager currently delivers Sponsored Products and will expand shortly into Display and Video as Tesco Media builds towards a more unified experience across its media ecosystem. Over time, AI powered workflows and recommendations will help advertisers reduce manual tasks, uncover new opportunities and make faster optimisation decisions, while greater interoperability will allow agencies and brands to connect the platform with the tools they already use.
The aim is to make control feel enabling rather than burdensome, giving brands simpler ways to create media that is timely, relevant and genuinely helpful to customers. The infrastructure behind Ad Manager is powered by Kevel, a specialist provider of API first ad technology for retailers and commerce media networks and designed to help Tesco Media deliver a seamless advertising experience across its digital channels.
JULES
JULES, a French menswear retailer with over 350 stores across France and owned by Association Familiale Mulliez, has selected Ekinops solutions as it looks to modernise web security and better support its evolving digital usage.
Based in Roubaix and employing 2,800 people, JULES was looking for a replacement solution capable of providing greater visibility into internet usage, making filtering policies easier to manage and strengthening employee protection against web-based risks, without compromising user experience.
It says it selected Ekinops’ solution for its performance, ease of integration into the existing information system, its ability to facilitate the migration of filtering rules, the quality of website categorisation and the availability of clear dashboards enabling more effective monitoring of usage, blocks and risks. Ekinops’ positioning as a French software provider was also an important criterion, in line with requirements for sovereignty, proximity, GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) compliance and trust in data management.
Morrisons
Just Eat is expanding its autonomous delivery robot trial with Starship Technologies to Cambourne in Cambridgeshire. This is the first trial location where it doesn't already offer grocery delivery and builds on Sunderland and Milton Keynes deployments.
Morrisons has become one of the first grocery brands to tap the technology, with benefits including adding delivery capacity in the run up to the festive season and during offers such as the regular 'Half Price Wednesdays' on Just Eat. The Cambourne supermarket which is now live is the fourth Morrisons to begin autonomous robot deliveries with three Morrisons Dailys live across Sunderland and Milton Keynes.
THG Commerce
THG Commerce, part of THG Ingenuity, has integrated Criteo Sponsored Products into its AI Shopping Assistant, built using Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise. THG Commerce says it is the first commerce technology provider in Europe to bring Criteo Sponsored Products into AI powered conversational search, opening up a new retail media opportunity for retailers and brands.
Retailers can now monetise customer conversations through relevant sponsored product placements. The integration places sponsored and organic product recommendations side by side within the same conversation. Brands can reach shoppers in AI driven discovery moments, when intent is high and recommendations are shaped by the shopper's own words. Early results show sponsored products surfaced through the AI Shopping Assistant reached a click-through rate more than five times the average, and a conversion rate more than double the average.
The AI Shopping Assistant draws keywords and filters from each conversation and turns them into tailored product recommendations. When a Criteo Sponsored Product is eligible and relevant, it appears clearly labelled within the assistant's response alongside organic recommendations, adding to the discovery experience rather than interrupting it.
The same relevance models that power Criteo search advertising, including keyword matching, semantic understanding and strict relevance thresholds, apply in the conversational context. Sponsored recommendations appear only when they match what the shopper has asked for.
The integration builds on THG Ingenuity’s broader partnership with Criteo and on its wider collaboration with Google Cloud. THG Commerce has developed a suite of agentic commerce solutions built on Gemini Enterprise. Alongside the AI Shopping Assistant, these include the AI Stylist, which offers AI powered virtual try-on for beauty, apparel and footwear, and Shopping Assistant Insights, which is available in Gemini Enterprise and helps retailers understand what their shoppers want and how the assistant is serving them. Each is delivered as a plug and play SaaS service, available through Google Cloud Marketplace and able to operate independently of the underlying storefront.

Morrisons taps Logile to enhance store planning across supermarket, convenience, logistics sites
Morrisons has selected Logile as it looks to enhance store workload planning across the UK grocery retailer’s business. The agreement covers its supermarket and convenience store estate alongside its logistics network.
Morrisons is implementing Logile software in a bid to simplify central planning, replacing time-consuming manual spreadsheets with optimised operational data and intelligence. By delivering clearer visibility into store workload requirements, it says that central operations can provide accurate, reliable insight across the estate, allowing teams to focus on better supporting store operations.
“Getting colleagues where customers need them most is the heart of what we do, and at our scale you need a reliable, shared foundation to get that right,” says Alex Rose, Head of Productivity at Morrisons. “A large supermarket and a local convenience store operate differently so our planning has to flex to those local needs while keeping central support consistent. When our store managers have plans they can depend on, they spend less time managing admin and more time supporting their colleagues and serving customers.”
John Lewis, Asda, Morrisons, H&M, Dunelm, and Waitrose among 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards finalists
We're hugely pleased to present the finalists and shortlists for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards, sponsored by 3D Cloud, Business France, and Retail Technology Show 2027. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.

AI powered marketing platform Miracly publicly launches with $2 million pre-seed funding round
Miracly, a GEO and AI operating system for marketing teams and agencies developed by The Wild Ventures, the company behind Scandinavian home decor brand Wild Palace, has announced a $2 million pre-seed round led by Beenext Ventures and Lotus alongside a Swedish family office, with existing investors including Stefan Lindeberg, Founder at VC firm Creandum; Alex Bouaziz, Founder and CEO at Deel; Thomas Ekman, Founder at 6GAI and former CEO at Axel Johnson publ, Dustin and Tele2; Hedda Baverud Olsson, Founder and CEO at Lassie, and Parham Benisi, Partner at Pophouse.
The company publicly launched last week. Pre-launch it has landed customers including Dreams, Acclime, Pixi Beauty, Andy Okay and Duellix.
“We’re seeing an incredible demand for Miracly’s AI marketing platform. Companies all over the world are impacted by decreasing organic traffic from Google and increasing cost of performance marketing,” says Bjorn Bergstrom, Co-founder at Miracly.
“We started out with GEO analytics and AI content generation, but are rapidly becoming a holistic AI marketing platform based on the demand and opportunity we’re seeing in the market. Marketing and agency teams are becoming hybrid marketing and tech organisations and need to develop incredibly quickly to keep up with the changes. Miracly is here to guide them through this shift into an AI first era with completely customised recommendations and agentic flows.”
Vestiaire Collective becomes first luxury resale platform to standardise new listing photos with AI
Photoroom has published results from its work with Vestiaire Collective, a platform for pre-loved luxury fashion. Vestiaire Collective split its new listings into two random groups. One had its main photo edited by Photoroom, the other by the photo clipping tool Vestiaire Collective built in-house years ago. Listings in the Photoroom group sold at a 5% higher rate of liquidity. Their product pages drew 3 to 7% more unique views, with bags and shoes gaining the most.
Vestiaire Collective says it chose Photoroom after testing several generative AI tools and finding that every one of them changed the items. A photo that changes the item breaks two things on a resale platform. Vestiaire Collective authenticates a share of items from their photos alone, checking labels, stitching and how light falls on the material. Buyers can also return anything that turns out to be fake or has a fault the seller didn't disclose. Smooth out a scuff or redraw a logo and both are at risk.
Photoroom's own testing points the same way. In a benchmark of 4,250 AI generated images across 850 real products, the best AI image editing models on the market passed a full product fidelity check only 29% of the time. 63% of UK consumers say inconsistent product images or branding make a marketplace less trustworthy, according to Photoroom's State of GenAI in Marketplaces 2026 report.
Tomáš Čupr bags $32 million for Duvo, an AI platform born from challenges he encountered while building Rohlik
Duvo, an automation platform that gives teams an AI workforce for their day-to-day operations, has announced a $32 million Series A led by Balderton Capital, with participation from existing investors Index Ventures, Northzone and Credo Ventures. The round brings its total funding to $48 million and will fund its expansion, starting with retailers and CPG companies.
Michael Green is also joining from Databricks as Senior Vice President, Go-to-Market. He previously served as a Senior Vice President at Salesforce. Spencer Insolia recently came onboard as Managing Director, US. He was previously President at Kmart and a Managing Director at Accenture. Christoph Schwaiger, former CEO at Aldi South Holdings, has also signed on as Senior Advisor for Europe.
"For a while I measured AI in heads, counting how many people an agent could replace. It's the wrong unit," says Tomáš Čupr, Co-founder and CEO at Duvo and Founder and Group CEO at Rohlik Group. "At Rohlik, the gains I'd point to came from work nobody had the hours for. Our planners used to check about eight at-risk products a day per market for shortages. Now every signal gets checked, around the clock. We think of it as raising the GDP of every employee: more value from the people a company has, not the same value from fewer of them."
Kingfisher raids European home improvement retailer OBI to bring in Sebastian Gundel as CEO
Kingfisher, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, has announced the appointment of Sebastian Gundel as Chief Executive Officer, effective 1st February 2027. He will join Kingfisher’s board of directors on the same date.
He brings more than two decades of leadership experience in the home improvement sector, including as Chief Executive Officer at European retailer OBI, where he led the company's evolution from traditional retail to a digitally enabled, customer centric, omnichannel business.
Prior to becoming CEO, he served as Chief Customer & Digital Officer, leading OBI's omnichannel transformation and digital innovation agenda. His responsibilities spanned loyalty, marketplaces and ecosystem development, as well as the expansion of trade propositions.
Claudia Arney, Chair, says: “Following a thorough selection process, the board is delighted to appoint Sebastian as Chief Executive Officer. Sebastian combines deep experience in home improvement retail and clear expertise in Kingfisher’s strategic growth drivers with a strong track record of innovation and operational delivery. He will build on the significant progress made under Thierry Garnier’s leadership while bringing fresh perspectives as we continue to evolve the business. Sebastian has the board’s full support as he leads Kingfisher through its next phase of growth and value creation.”

items.body:
Pixel Inspiration and dunnhumby deliver Sony BRAVIA powered retail media roll-out for Booker Wholesale
Booker Wholesale has deployed more than 500 Sony BRAVIA Professional Displays to establish a new retail media network across 100 of its UK locations. The project was delivered by Pixel Inspiration in partnership with dunnhumby.
Installed predominantly at rack ends and above palletised merchandise, the displays provide a platform for targeted advertising and promotional content, while integrating into the existing wholesale environment. This presented specific challenges for the installation. Displays needed to be positioned for maximum visibility while also being protected against accidental impacts from stock movement, pallet handling and day-to-day warehouse operations.
Sony BZ35L BRAVIA Professional Displays were selected as part of the hardware solution to provide the combination of image quality, reliability and operational efficiency required for the network. To provide additional protection, Pixel Inspiration worked with UNICOL to develop a combined mounting and protective shroud solution. This was designed to withstand the demands of a busy cash and carry environment while maintaining appropriate airflow and ventilation around the displays.
The displays use Sony’s Android-based System on Chip (SoC) technology, reducing the need for additional external media players and helping simplify the overall installation. The network is managed through the DISE content management system, enabling campaign content to be centrally targeted and distributed across Booker’s national estate.
Sony Remote Device Manager is also used to monitor the displays remotely, carry out firmware updates and undertake maintenance tasks. This helps reduce the need for onsite intervention and supports efficient management of the large scale display network.
“Booker’s nationwide retail media network is a great example of how digital signage is evolving to create new opportunities for brands to engage customers in highly relevant environments," says Karl Ingham, Key Account Manager, Sony Professional Displays and Solutions Europe.
"This deployment demonstrates the scalability and versatility of Sony’s display technology, while the combination of high quality visuals, remote device management and reliable performance makes it well suited to the demands of a busy wholesale environment. We’re delighted to support Booker and Pixel Inspiration in creating a platform that can deliver value for both Booker’s customers and its brand partners."
